say.en: Why do families who work so hard stay poor for generations? Anees Jung points to a trap made of debt, fear and acceptance of fate. In this lesson: Explain the vicious circle that traps the bangle makers.
Compare Saheb and Mukesh.
Identify the central themes and the meaning of the title.

body.en: The bangle makers are trapped from two sides. Moneylenders, middlemen, the police, bureaucrats and politicians together keep them in debt and fear, so they dare not organise into a cooperative. At the same time, they accept their misery as fate handed down by birth, so they lose the will to resist. Poverty and acceptance feed each other.

points.en: Outside pressure: moneylenders, middlemen, police, officials, politicians
Inside pressure: belief in destiny and caste-bound work
Fear stops them from forming a cooperative
The result: poverty passes from generation to generation

say.en: At the centre is the loss of childhood, the spring of life.
Poverty passes from one generation to the next.
Children work in garbage dumps and beside furnaces.
Middlemen, moneylenders and officials exploit the workers.
Many accept their suffering as fate and do not resist.
Saheb loses his freedom when he takes a job.
Mukesh's dream of driving a car is a sign of hope.

body.en: Both parts show stolen childhood, poverty, child labour and exploitation. Yet the two boys differ at the end: Saheb gives up his freedom for a wage, while Mukesh insists on being his own master and dares to dream. The title links spring, the season of growth, to childhood that has been lost.

problem.en: Compare and contrast Saheb and Mukesh.

steps.en: Similarities: both are poor children denied education and childhood.
Saheb: ragpicker; later takes a tea-stall job and loses his freedom.
Mukesh: from a bangle-making family; wants to be a motor mechanic.
Conclude: Saheb accepts servitude, while Mukesh dares to break free.

answer.en: Both boys are victims of poverty and child labour, but Saheb ends up giving up his independence for a wage, while Mukesh insists on being his own master and dreams of a different life.
